items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: He must have been about 20 or 21 when he was playing with Parker.

ctx.x: I think Miles Davis was about 20... He must have been about 20 or 21 when he was playing with Parker.
I think Parker helped him when he was just a kid. Because he came to Juilliard quite young. And then he got tired of that job. I mean, that wonderful music school.

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: So we'd buy Dizzy Gillespie records and Charlie Parker records and we'd rehearse them.

ctx.x: You were talking about Clarence Ford and you know how?

Oh yeah, yeah. So we was playing bebop. So we'd buy Dizzy Gillespie records and Charlie Parker records and we'd rehearse them. And we'd call, the name of the band was Wallace Devin Bode and his bebop jockeys. And we, I called all those old musicians up and told them I didn't talk with them anymore. So. How did that go over? Bad. Bad. Because I wasn't making any money. I bought a house. And I was fixing to lose my house. Didn't have any food to eat. Didn't have any food to eat. My wife, she was Jean, she was just…
